title: Six-week pulse and priority reset (midyear) v0.1
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures the six-week midyear pulse, a lightweight reset for company-level priorities and a proposed agenda for a shorter, decision-focused all-hands. The goal: surface high-risk tradeoffs, land 3 clear company objectives for the next quarter of work, and create a 6-week action map with owners and measurable checkpoints.

Context / Why now:
- We are at the midpoint between Q2 and Q3 planning windows; several teams report drift from original OKRs due to new enterprise contracts and capacity work for Private deployments.
- Observability and cost signals show rising token unit costs for a subset of hosted endpoints (notable on chat-heavy customers).
- Leadership wants a nimble, cross-functional reset rather than a full OKR rewrite — reduce noise and enable execution.

Summary recommendation (TL;DR):
- Keep company mission and top-level thesis same; focus the reset on three outcome-driven objectives for the next 6–12 weeks: reliability (SLO/RCA), cost/perf (Optimize), and sales-to-delivery throughput (Dedicated/Private onboarding).
- Run a 45-minute all-hands with a 20-minute leadership brief, 10-minute demo slice, and a 15-minute decision workshop.
- Implement an action map with clear owners and weekly checkpoints; require product/eng/legal signoffs for any objective that impacts enterprise timelines.

Proposed Company Objectives (6–12wk focused):
O1: Reduce customer-facing latency and error surface for hosted API top 20 customers.
  KR1: Decrease 95th-percentile end-user latency from 420ms to <=300ms for top-20 endpoints (measured at token emission)
  KR2: Reduce active error rate (5xx + throttles) by 60% on the same endpoints
  KR3: Two production rollouts: KV-cache tuning + routing policy tweak; both with rollback plans and tracing enabled

O2: Improve inference unit economics for conversational workloads by targeted optimization.
  KR1: Reduce per-token cost on high-concurrency chat by 18% through batching + quantization profiles
  KR2: Pilot Redwood Optimize suggestions on three pilot customers and measure cost delta and quality regression (metric: pass rate on eval set >=95%)
  KR3: Publish internal playbook for choosing batching/quantization per workload

O3: Shorten enterprise time-to-live (TTOnboarding) for Dedicated/Private deals.
  KR1: Reduce average POC->GA time from 12 weeks to 8 weeks for 70% of upcoming deals
  KR2: Deliver a hardened private-deploy template (VPC+KMS) and one on-prem integration checklist
  KR3: Launch a Professional Services runbook and price card for standard installs

Notes on objective selection: these map to revenue protection (O3), customer experience (O1), and unit economics (O2). Each objective requires a cross-functional owner (product + eng + SRE + solutions).

Decision points for leadership workshop (all-hands interactive segment):
- Priority ordering if we can only fully resource two objectives: do we prioritize reliability (O1) or cost/perf (O2)?
- Allocate one small engineering pod (4 FTE) to accelerate Dedicated onboarding vs. fund additional SRE capacity for hosted API alerts — which is higher impact?
- Authorize a temporary runway of up to $150k for external contractor support for on-prem integrations (if needed).

All-hands (45 min) proposed run-of-show:
- 00:00–00:05: Quick context + where we are (CEO)
- 00:05–00:25: Leadership brief (three slides: objectives, current signals, ask) (Product + Eng leads)
- 00:25–00:35: Short demo — observable charts + one customer story where reliability mattered (SRE + CS)
- 00:35–00:45: Interactive decision workshop (live polling + breakout Q&A for 5 minutes)
- Follow-up: publish meeting minutes and action map in company Confluence page within 48 hours

Suggested audience prep (1-pager to send 3 days before):
- Snapshot dashboard (latency/error/cost top 20 endpoints)
- Short customer impact anecdotes (CS)
- List of asks with clear yes/no/maybe options for leadership to vote on

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Re-prioritization fatigue — teams may feel this is just another pause.
  Mitigation: Keep the reset timeboxed (6–12 weeks), and ensure changes are reversible (feature flags, rollout gates).
- Risk: Quality regression from aggressive quantization/batching
  Mitigation: Pilot with internal evals + canary on low-traffic customers; require objective quality thresholds.
- Risk: Sales expectations misaligned if we slow enterprise onboarding
  Mitigation: Communicate timeline to sales and provide a gating checklist for exceptions.

6-week action map (initial assignments):
- Asha (owner) — Run cadence, publish weekly pulse deck, coordinate leadership workshop (weekly checkpoint: Mon 09:30)
- Tom (eng-sre) — Build 95p latency dashboard, instrument top-20 endpoints, initial RCA on 3 highest-error routes (due: week 1)
- Morgan (product-hosted-api) — Draft Optimize pilot plan and pilot customer roster (due: week 1)
- Claire (solutions-eng) — Draft onboarding template for Dedicated/Private (due: week 2)
- Diego (sales-ops) — Freeze priority enterprise deals list and align expectations with account teams (due: week 1)
- Rina (finance) — Budget approval for contractor runway and cost model updates (due: week 2)

Communication & follow-up cadence:
- Weekly pulse deck (one slide each: metrics, blockers, asks) published every Monday by 11:00 PT
- Bi-weekly leadership checkpoint (30m) to surface escalation items and sign decisions
- Post-all-hands: confluence update + decision log + action map (within 48h)

Open questions (to land prior to all-hands):
1) Do we want to formally retire any Q2 company-level KRs that are now clearly unachievable? (proposal: retire quietly with documented rationale)
2) Can we commit the small eng pod (4 FTE) to Dedicated onboarding for 6–8 weeks if leadership votes yes?
3) What is the acceptance threshold for Optimize pilot quality regressions (suggested >=95% pass rate on our evals)?

Appendix — suggested slides for leadership brief (5 bullets per slide):
- Slide A: Current signals (latency, errors, cost, deal slippage) with simple trend lines
- Slide B: Proposed 3 objectives + why each matters (1 line rationale each)
- Slide C: Tradeoffs (resource map + timeline impacts)
- Slide D: Asks (clear decision choices and recommended options)
- Slide E: Next steps + owners

Notes to self / draft thoughts (informal):
- Keep the language concrete. Managers hate vague asks — give them clear yes/no choices.
- Lean on CS anecdote; humans remember stories more than numbers.
- We should avoid a 90-minute all-hands — shorter + focused = higher decision velocity.

Immediate next steps (this doc):
- Share with leadership (Asha) and request slot for 06/26 all-hands (deadline to confirm: 06/20)
- Ask product/eng leads to confirm owners and feasibility estimates by 06/13
- Prepare the pre-read 1-pager and dashboards by 06/23

Change log (v0.1):
- 2025-06-05 created initial outline
- 2025-06-12 added proposed KRs for Optimize pilot and Dedicated onboarding
- 2025-06-18 updated owners and timing after sync with SRE

-- end --
